newsitem.title: USA: Apple demonstrates new Macintosh features.
newsitem.headline: Apple demonstrates new Macintosh features.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc. Tuesday demonstrated a preliminary version of its new operating system for the Macintosh personal computer, which it claims is easier to use and has more Internet capabilities.

Apple officials said the Mac OS 8 operating system, also known as System 8, is expected to be released in July. System 8 is designed to provide significant improvements that will also run on its next-generation Rhapsody operating system, slated for release next year, they said.
Internet features are key for people using Macintosh computers to publish on the World Wide Web, said Jim Gable, vice president of product marketing at the Cupertino, Calif.-based computer maker.
"We're the publishing shop for the Internet," Gable said in a presentation at a conference in San Diego.
Apple, which has been struggling to return to stable profitability for the last 18 months, says more than 50 percent of the content on the Internet is created using its Macintosh computers.

Gable demonstrated a preliminary version of Mac OS 8 which he said will incorporate the company's recently announced Personal Web Sharing feature. Personal Web Sharing enables any Macintosh to become a mini-Web server so it can display Web pages to a small network, for example.

Web authors can simply drag and drop icons into a box to set up a Web page, he said. Another feature for those who do not have time to create full-blown Web pages allows computer users to generate Web pages on the fly from file folders.
A viewer can then be used to provide a display of what is in a folder on a network-connected Macintosh.
"I can actually share my entire system, if I want to, across the entire Internet with Personal Web Sharing, although I'm not certain I would recommend that to all people," he said.
Apple will bundle software from Palo Alto, Calif.-based Marimba, a start-up company whose product enables software to be updated over the Internet, in the new system release.

The new system, designed to enable multiple applications to operate at the same time, will also include an improved user interface aimed at helping reduce screen clutter when many applications and files are being displayed at once.

These can be stored as graphical tabs like file folder tabs at the bottom of a computer screen, or they can be closed up like a window shade, leaving just the software's name at the top of each application, to ease navigation.

The new operating system will also include a feature called the Apple Applet Runner, which enables it to run programmes in the Java programming language, developed by Sun Microsystems Inc., without having to download them first.

Microsoft Corp., whose Windows operating systems dominate the desktop computing market, is also integrating its operating system and applications software more seamlessly with the Internet and Web technologies.
